issues.t: Steering clunks, pops or catches when turning
issues.sym: A clunk, knock or pop from the front end when turning at low speed or parking, or a 'hitch' that you feel through the wheel every few degrees of turning. It often gets worse over time.
issues.why: Wear inside the steering rack is the most common finding, and dealers have replaced racks under warranty. Worn front strut bearings or the steering shaft joint can make a similar noise, so owners sometimes need more than one repair.
issues.next: Have a shop check the rack, tie rods, strut mounts and steering shaft with the car on the ground and the wheel being turned. Get it fixed promptly; a badly worn rack can make steering unpredictable.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil pan gasket
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the car and an oily, wet oil pan. The oil level may drop between changes.
issues.why: The sealant joint between the oil pan and the engine can seep. Owners report it from around 30,000 miles, and some were fixed under warranty.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and keep it topped up. Have the pan resealed before the leak gets worse or drips onto hot exhaust parts.

issues.sym: More vibration felt in the cabin at idle, a thunk when shifting or pulling away, or clunks over bumps.
issues.why: The rubber engine mounts wear out or tear over time, letting the engine move more than it should.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked, especially if the car vibrates more than it used to. Replacing a torn mount is a moderate job and prevents strain on hoses, exhaust and other mounts.

issues.t: Loud or noisy heater blower fan
issues.sym: The fan behind the dashboard gets loud, whines or rattles, especially at certain speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor bearings wear, or debris gets into the fan. Several early Mazda2s had the blower replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Have the cabin air filter and blower checked. If the motor itself is noisy, replacing it is the fix.

issues.sym: The engine dies while driving or won't restart, even with fuel in the tank.
issues.why: Owners have reported the in-tank fuel pump failing on early Mazda2s, some replaced under warranty.
issues.next: If the car stalls, get safely off the road. Have a shop test fuel pressure. Check for any open recall or warranty coverage before paying.

issues.t: Brake shudder from warped rotors or sticking calipers
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes when braking from speed, brakes creak or drag, or one front wheel gets very hot.
issues.why: Front brake rotors can wear unevenly and cause pulsing, and owners have also reported front calipers seizing at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Resurfacing or replacing the rotors usually cures shudder; a sticking caliper should be replaced right away because it wears pads fast and pulls the car.

issues.t: Manual clutch slave cylinder leaks, soft clutch or grinding shifts
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft or squeaks, gears grind (especially 2nd and 3rd) or are hard to get into.
issues.why: The clutch slave cylinder can leak or wear out, so the clutch doesn't fully release. Owners whose gears grind sometimes find the slave cylinder was the real cause.
issues.next: Have the clutch hydraulics checked before assuming the gearbox is bad. Replacing the slave cylinder and bleeding the system is a much smaller job than a transmission repair.

issues.t: Driver seat height links can crack (recall)
issues.sym: The driver seat feels loose, rocks or shifts, or doesn't hold its height.
issues.why: Links in the seat height adjuster can crack or separate, so the driver may not stay in a safe driving position. Mazda recalled 2011 Mazda2s, along with other models, to fix the seats.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the free repair done. If your seat feels loose, get it checked before driving any distance.

issues.t: Oil seeping from the oil pressure switch
issues.sym: Oil wetness around the oil pressure switch on the engine, or a low oil warning. Most likely in very cold climates.
issues.why: Lots of short starts in extreme cold can make the original oil pressure switch leak. Mazda released a more durable switch.
issues.next: Have the switch area checked during an oil change. If it is wet, replace the switch; it is a small part.

issues.t: Rear creak or squeak over bumps
issues.sym: A creaking or squeaking from the back of the car when going over bumps.
issues.why: The rear shock absorber rod can stick to the rubber bump stop, or the bump stop can stick to its mount.
issues.next: Have the rear shocks and bump stops checked. Mazda has a bulletin for this, and some owners solve it by lubricating the bump stops.

issues.t: Airbag light from a loose connector under the seat
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and off.
issues.why: Owners have traced intermittent airbag lights to a loose wiring connector under the driver seat.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read and the under-seat connectors checked. Airbags may not work properly while the light is on.

issues.t: Check engine light from a frozen fuel tank breather hose
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on in winter with a fuel tank pressure sensor code.
issues.why: Snow and ice can block the fuel tank breather hose. Mazda's fix is a longer hose and new clip.
issues.next: Have the code read. If it is the tank pressure code, ask the dealer about the updated hose.

issues.t: Exhaust squeak at idle or shutoff
issues.sym: A squeak from under the car at idle or right when you turn off the engine, usually heard from outside.
issues.why: A seal ring in the exhaust can rub against the catalytic converter as the engine vibrates. Mazda says it causes no damage or leak.
issues.next: Nothing needs to be done if this is the only symptom. Have a shop look if you also hear a rattle or smell exhaust.

issues.sym: Rattles or creaks from the dashboard, passenger floor, headliner or sun visors, especially on rough roads.
issues.why: Plastic panels and trim can rattle as the car ages. Mazda issued a bulletin for a passenger-side floor rattle on rough roads.
issues.next: Note exactly where and when the rattle happens and have a shop add felt tape or re-clip loose trim.

issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the front over small bumps.
issues.why: The small links connecting the anti-roll bar to the suspension can wear out early.
issues.next: Have the links checked; they are quick to replace.

issues.t: Radio cuts out with no sound
issues.sym: The radio display stays on but the sound cuts out, no matter whether you use radio, CD or AUX.
issues.why: An owner report ties this to faulty factory radio units that were not recalled.
issues.next: Check fuses and connections first. If the head unit itself has failed, a replacement radio is the fix.

issues.sym: A headlight flickers or stops working, and the plug may look melted.
issues.why: Water can get into the headlight wiring connector, causing a short and heat damage.
issues.next: Have the bulb plug and harness inspected. Replace a melted connector rather than just the bulb.

issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the car, a sweet smell, or the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: Owners report the radiator leaking at higher mileage.
issues.next: Check the coolant level and don't drive if the engine overheats. A leaking radiator is usually replaced.

issues.sym: Harsh, jerky or delayed shifts, or noise from the transmission.
issues.why: Owners have reported rough shifting and noise on 2014 automatics. Low or old fluid can cause similar symptoms.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked and the transmission codes read before agreeing to major repairs.
